evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.245: brevior ipse quam testis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Short in length, and of people short in stature (Cic., Quint.); in classical prose parvus is “small”, not “short” (Lewis & Short). The opposite is longus (see long).
Short because something has been cut off or is missing.

phrases.latin: hic brevis ingentem comminus ībit aprum
phrases.english: this short one will go at a huge boar at close quarters

phrases.latin: Brācae tibi jam breviōrēs sunt; crēvistī.
phrases.english: Your trousers are too short now: you’ve grown.
